features.title: Skeleton project generator (finished 2026-11-25)
features.body:
A File menu item opens a panel where the user sets the project defaults (title, BPM, ticks per line, time signature), the key of the song, and a chord progression (typed, or inserted as blocks from presets). *Create* replaces the open project with a new one. If a progression was given, the project gets a bass and a piano module, each with a pattern that follows the chords: the bass plays each chord's root, the piano plays all notes of the chord.

Decided by the owner on 2026-11-25:

- **Panel, not an OS window.** The generator opens as an in-app overlay panel, like the Appearance panel. Dracker stays a single-window app.
- **The panel is modal.** A click outside it does not close it and nothing behind it reacts; only *Create*, *Cancel*, or Escape close it (T20).
- **Time signature is a project setting.** It is saved in the project file and drives beat and bar highlighting in the pattern editor, the timeline, and the count-in.
- **Chord input accepts both forms.** Roman numerals relative to the key (`ii`, `V7`) and chord names (`Dm7`, `G7`) in the same field.
- **Confirm before replacing.** If the open project has unsaved changes, the generator asks before discarding them.
- **Proposals accepted.** All proposals of T01–T08 were approved as written (see *Done*). The feature is not built yet, so these decisions are recorded in the *Done* entries below; T26 moves them into `docs/manual.md` and `../architecture.md`.

Facts about the current code that the tasks rely on:

- The File menu is native (`source/platform/macos/appkit.d` → `MENU_ITEMS`). A menu click is sent as a key press, so every item needs its own key binding and a `StudioAction` value.
- The project file stores the time signature and key (T12) and the session exposes them (`linesPerBeat()`, `linesPerBar()`, `songKey()`, undoable `doSetTimeSignature()` / `doSetKey()`; T15). The count-in (one bar, at least 2 beats; T29), the pattern editor's row shading and the timeline's grid, ruler and snapping (T17) follow the time signature, which the transport bar's **SIG** control sets (T18).
- A pattern track plays one note at a time, so a chord needs one track per note. A cell names its module (`NoteCell.moduleId`); a track with no module set is silent.
- `doAddModule` does not wire the module; wires are added separately. No presets ship with the app (`resources/` holds only fonts).
- Available building blocks: `StudioSession.openProjectFromMemory()` (T10); `openConfirmDialog()` and modal overlays (`Widget.isModalOverlay()`, T09); `StudioRoot.confirmDiscardThen()` (T27); `app.music_theory` (T11); `app.skeleton_gen` instrument choices, `resolveInstrument()`, `audioOutputPort()` (T13); `app.chord_progression` (`parseProgression()`, `resolveChord()`, `chordLabel()`, `chordIntervals()`, `ChordBlock.halfBars`; T14; presets `PROGRESSION_PRESETS`, `presetsFor()`, `presetBlocks()`, `presetLabel()`; T16); `SkeletonSpec`, `validateSpec()`, `generateSkeleton()` (T19); `StudioRoot.openSkeletonPanel()` and `SkeletonPanel` with its `onCreate` hook (T20–T22; `onCreate` is connected by `StudioRoot`, T24; the File menu item and ⇧⌘N open the panel, T23).

features.title: Pattern editor views (tracker, piano roll, drumpad)
features.body:
The pattern editor gets a top bar that switches between three views of the current pattern: the existing **Tracker** view, a DAW-style **Piano roll**, and an FL-Studio-style **Drumpad** for drum patterns. Drum patterns are a new pattern type. All views use the app's high-contrast theme and its rules (contrast ratios, color-blind-safe sets, a non-color cue for every color meaning, no size changes).

Decided by the owner on 2026-11-25:

- **Piano roll is a view of the same pattern.** It shows and edits the same cells as the tracker view. Overlapping notes go on different tracks; a track is added automatically when a note needs one. No change to playback or to how notes are stored.
- **Piano roll shows one module at a time.** A module picker in its bar chooses the module; its notes are drawn in full, other modules' notes dimmed behind them; new notes go to the picked module.
- **Drum pattern = cell grid + lane table.** A drum pattern is a normal cell grid in which each track is one drum lane, plus a lane table (name, module, note per lane) and a "drum" type flag, saved in a new optional file section. The engine plays it unchanged.
- **A lane triggers any module + note.** One drum pattern can mix a Kicker, DrumSynth sounds and Sampler hits.
- **Views per type.** Normal patterns offer Tracker and Piano roll. Drum patterns offer Drumpad and Tracker.
- **Creating.** "New drum pattern" (with lanes for a default kit), and conversion between normal and drum patterns in both directions.

Facts about the current code that the tasks rely on:

- `PatternEditorView` (`source/gui/views/pattern_editor.d`, about 2,100 lines) is one widget holding the header controls (pattern dropdown, tracks and lines boxes, add / duplicate / delete), the tracker grid, selection, clipboard and note entry. It has no notion of views.
- `SavedPattern` is `patternId, tracks, lines, name, cells`; the `PATS` file section is a fixed sequence, so new per-pattern data needs a new optional section (as was done for `MIDI` and `MUSC`).
- A track plays one note at a time; a note lasts until the next note or note-off on its track; each cell names its module. The piano roll must derive note lengths from that.
- The DrumSynth is an 8-voice GM-mapped kit (one drum per MIDI note); the Kicker is a single drum; the Sampler plays loaded samples.
- The theme has tokens for tracker rows and fields but none for piano keys, roll notes or pads. Every new color must pass the contrast and color-vision checks in `tests/unit/appearance_test.d` for every built-in palette.

features.title: Instrument library in the patchbay
features.body:
The patchbay gets a sidebar on its left that lists presets for modules, grouped (instruments and effects). A set of presets ships with the app; the user's own presets appear in the same list.

Decided by the owner on 2026-11-25:

- **All presets, grouped.** The list shows every preset (instruments and effects) in groups.
- **Adding: double-click and drag, no auto-wiring.** Double-click adds the module at the next free position; dragging onto the canvas adds it where it is dropped. Neither wires it.
- **User presets live in an app-wide folder.** `~/Library/Application Support/Dracker/Instruments`. "Add to Instruments" on a module saves its preset there; `.msym` files placed there also appear.
- **Bundled set.** About 12 instruments and about 4 effects, designed in this project and approved by the owner by ear.
- **The skeleton generator uses the library.** Its Bass and Piano menus list the library's playable instruments; its defaults become the bundled Electric Bass and Electric Piano.

Facts about the current code that the tasks rely on:

- A preset file (`.msym`) holds one module: a synth, an effect, or a MetaModule with an inner patch. It has a preset name but no category field. `StudioContext.saveModulePreset()` / `loadModulePreset()` / `applyModulePreset()` and the patchbay menu items exist.
- `PatchbayView` fills its whole pane with the canvas; there is no sidebar. Modules are added from the canvas context menu (`addModuleAt`).
- The toolkit has no list widget and no drag-and-drop between widgets.
- No presets ship with the app. Fonts are the model for bundled resources: `bundledFontDirectories()` looks in `Contents/Resources/Fonts` and `resources/fonts`; `packaging/macos/bundle_macos.sh` builds the bundle.
- The skeleton generator has its default bass and piano as constants in `source/app/skeleton_gen.d` and a `--sound-check` render for listening.

features.title: Composition helper (`dracker-compose`)
features.body:
A second program, built from the same source tree, that writes Dracker project files (`.msv`) and module preset files (`.msym`) without the app. It exists so that an agent can compose music for Dracker. The same script language is also offered to the user inside the app, in a **Script** tab of the pattern editor (decided 2026-11-26, T108; tasks T109–T114). It has two main parts: the **module writer** (choose a base module, set its parameters, save a `.msym`) and the **project writer** (project properties, modules made with the module writer, wires, patterns, parts, chords, arrangement, save a `.msv`).

Decided by the owner on 2026-11-26:

- **Driven by a command script.** A plain-text script of commands run in order, one per line. Each command maps to one function of the core library.
- **A separate program in the same repository.** A second executable from the same package and source tree, without GUI or audio-device code, so it always matches the app's file format and module list.
- **Supporting functions.** A catalog (module types, ports, parameters, bundled presets, chord syntax), describing an existing `.msv` / `.msym` as script text, editing existing projects with the same commands, and rendering to WAV with a report. Checking a script for errors is always available.
- **Parts first, tracker level available.** Music is mainly written for a named part (an instrument) at bar and beat positions with note lengths; the helper picks tracker tracks. Exact track and line placement stays available.
- **Proposals accepted.** All proposals of T66–T71 were approved as written by the owner on 2026-11-26 (see *Done*); they are recorded in the *Done* entries until T89 moves them into `docs/manual.md` and `../architecture.md`.

Architecture (the core knows nothing about its front ends, so the command line and the app's Script tab share it):

| Layer | Where | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core library | `source/compose/` (new) | Module writer, project writer, parts, chords, drums, arrangement. Works on documents in memory; knows nothing about scripts, files of commands, or the terminal. Every problem is returned as data (what, where, a suggestion), never printed. |
| Command interpreter | `source/compose/script/` (new) | Turns one command at a time into core calls and keeps the state between commands (the project being built, named modules and parts). It takes commands from any source, so a script file is just one way to feed it. |
| Program | `source/compose_main.d` (new) | The `dracker-compose` command line: run or check a script, catalog, describe, render. Reads files, prints results, sets the exit code. |
| Script tab in the app | `source/gui/views/script_view.d` (new) | A fourth tab of the pattern editor: the user types script lines and clicks Apply. Another front end feeding the same interpreter, started from a copy of the open project; the result is swapped in as one undo step, or nothing changes when a line fails (T108). |

Facts about the current code that the tasks rely on:

- Reusable as they are: `io.project_format` (documents, `.msv` / `.msym` reading and writing, validation), `graph.registry` (module types, ports, parameters with names, ranges and defaults; option names for every choice parameter (T91); parameters whose values are counts have none), `app.music_theory` (keys, scales, note names), `app.chord_progression` (chord and progression parser, chord notes, preset progressions), `app.pattern_notes` (placing notes on tracker tracks without collisions), `app.factory_presets` and `app.instrument_library` (bundled and user presets), `app.session` (trial activation of a document, offline render).
- A pattern track plays one note at a time; a note ends at the next note or note-off on its track; each cell names its module. `app.pattern_notes` already hides this for the piano roll.
- Drum patterns are a pattern kind with a lane table (name, module, note per track).
- A project's time signature fixes lines per beat and per bar (a line is a sixteenth note); the key is stored with the project.
- `dub.json` has three configurations: `app` and `headless` share `source/main.d`; `compose` builds `dracker-compose` (T72). Its entry point is in `source/compose_main.d` under `version (ComposeProgram)`. A file named as `mainSourceFile` of one configuration is left out of the others, so the `compose` configuration names none and excludes `source/main.d` instead; that keeps `compose_main.d` in the headless tests.
- Samples (Sampler), drawn curves and MetaModule child projects are stored inside a module's extra data; the app builds them through `StudioSession` (`doLoadSample`, `setMetaModuleChildProject`).
- Available building blocks for the helper: `compose.timing` (positions `bar`/`bar.beat`/`bar.beat.sixteenth` counted from 1 inside one pattern (see T90), lengths in beats, bars (`2b`) and lines (`3l`), and conversion to and from lines for a time signature; T73). `compose.module_writer` (`ModuleWriter`: a module from a type, a preset or a `.msym`; parameters set by name or option name and checked against the range; a `SavedModule`, .msym` bytes and files; every refusal as data with the nearest valid name; copies independent; names follow the instrument library rule; T74, T92). `compose.names` (name matching without regard to case or spaces and the nearest-name suggestion, shared by the whole helper; T92).

tasks.title: Module writer: Sampler samples
tasks.task: Load audio files (the formats the app's sample import accepts) into Sampler slots with root note and key range, producing the same stored data as the app, so the preset plays identically there. Tests compare against a preset saved through `StudioSession`.
tasks.done: 2026-11-26. ModuleWriter can now load audio bytes or files into Sampler slots with a root note and key range (loadSampleBytes/loadSampleFile), producing byte-identical extra data to the app. Added samplerExtraWithSample in sampler.d, and StudioSession.doLoadSample now calls it so both paths sanitize non-finite samples, per owner decision #1. Tests cover identity for one slot, two slots and a float.nan WAV, the byte layout, every refusal, file loading, round trips and copy independence. Recorded in docs/changelog.md (2026-11-26 22:18:09 KST).
tasks.guide:
**Goal.** `ModuleWriter` can load an audio file (or its bytes) into one of the 16 Sampler slots with a root note and a key range. The extra data is then byte for byte what the app stores after `StudioSession.doLoadSample`. Left out: loop points, envelopes, clearing a slot, reading a sample back as text, commands in `compose_main.d`.

**Read first.**
1. `source/app/session.d`: `doLoadSample` (3097-3145), `doSetModuleExtra` (3066-3080), `saveModulePresetToBytes` (1956-1970). The app's sequence and size limit (line 3070).
2. `source/modules/synths/sampler.d`: `SamplerSlotAsset` (49-71), `createFromPlanar` (101-145), `createSamplerAssetFromMemory` (198-210), `serializeExtra` (537-598), `deserializeExtra` (639-735), `swapAsset` (915-929). The byte layout.
3. `source/io/audio_io.d`: `decodeAudioMemory` (258-268), `deinterleaveToPlanar` (493-531). Mono is copied to both channels.
4. `source/compose/module_writer.d`: `ModuleProblemKind` (78-93), `ModuleEditResult` (151-154), `ModuleWriter` (170-186), `isNameProblem` (798-817), `readPresetFile` (1605-1612). How problems are returned; how an unsafe call is wrapped.
5. `tests/unit/compose_module_test.d`: `writerOf` (115), session test (557-605).

**Existing code to use.**
```d
SamplerSlotAsset* createSamplerAssetFromMemory(const(ubyte)[] bytes, out string err, ubyte rootNote = 60)
```
`sampler.d:198`. Null on failure, `err` set. Not `@safe`, not `nothrow`. Sets range 0..127, loop 0..frames.
```d
bool deserializeExtra(const(ubyte)[] payload, float sampleRate)
bool swapAsset(uint slot, void* newAsset, out void* oldAsset)
bool serializeExtra(out ubyte[] payload) const
static void destroyErased(void* raw)
```
`sampler.d:639`, `915`, `537`, `153`. `deserializeExtra` is false on bad data and ignores `sampleRate`. `swapAsset` is false when `slot >= 16`; the caller frees `oldAsset` with `SamplerSlotAsset.destroyErased`.
```d
enum size_t MAX_SLOTS = 16;
enum size_t MAX_EXTRA_BLOB_BYTES = 64u * 1024u * 1024u;
```
`sampler.d:494` (in `Sampler`); `io/project_format.d:66` (67,108,864).
```d
bool saveModulePresetToBytes(uint modId, string presetName, out ubyte[] bytes, out string err)
bool doLoadSample(uint samplerId, uint slot, const(ubyte)[] audioBytes, ubyte rootNote, ubyte lowNote,
        ubyte highNote, out string err)
```
`session.d:1956`, `3097`. False with `err` set. Tests only.

Nothing needed is private in `session.d`: lines 3110-3139 call only public `sampler.d` code.

**Write.**
In `sampler.d`, after the closing brace of `struct Sampler` (line 946):
```d
bool samplerExtraWithSample(const(ubyte)[] currentExtra, uint slot, const(ubyte)[] audioBytes,
        ubyte rootNote, ubyte lowNote, ubyte highNote, out ubyte[] blob, out string err)
```
It repeats `doLoadSample` without a session:
1. Refuse `slot >= Sampler.MAX_SLOTS || lowNote > highNote || highNote > 127 || rootNote > 127` with `err = "Target is not a Sampler slot"`.
2. `createSamplerAssetFromMemory(audioBytes, err, rootNote)`; on null return false.
3. Set `asset.lowNote` and `asset.highNote`. Set every sample of `asset.left` and `asset.right` that fails `isFinite` to `0.0f` (`createSamplerAssetFromMemory` does not sanitize samples; `createFromPlanar` does at lines 121-123, so doing it here guarantees neither the app nor `ModuleWriter` stores NaN samples).
4. `Sampler temp;`. If `currentExtra.length > 0` and `temp.deserializeExtra(currentExtra, 44_100.0f)` is false: free the asset, `err = "Existing sampler data could not be decoded"`, return false.
5. `temp.swapAsset(slot, asset, old)`; free `old` when not null; if `!temp.serializeExtra(blob)`, set `err = "Sampler data could not be serialized"` and return false; else return true.

In `module_writer.d`, at the end of `ModuleProblemKind`:
```d
    notASampler = 14,
    unreadableSample = 15,
    sampleTooLarge = 16
```
New public members of `ModuleWriter`:
```d
ModuleEditResult loadSampleBytes(int slot, const(ubyte)[] audioBytes, int rootNote = 60, int lowNote = 0,
        int highNote = 127) @safe nothrow
ModuleEditResult loadSampleFile(int slot, string path, int rootNote = 60, int lowNote = 0,
        int highNote = 127) @safe nothrow
```
Defaults are the app's (`gui/views/sample_editor.d:344`). Checks, in order: `desc_ is null` gives `notLoadedProblem()`; `mod_.typeId != "synth.sampler"` gives `notASampler`; slot outside 0..15, then root, low, high outside 0..127 give `outOfRange` with the nearest valid integer as text in `suggestion`; `lowNote > highNote` gives `outOfRange` with `highNote` as text in `suggestion`. A decoder or file failure gives `unreadableSample` with the reason `"could not load the sample: " ~ err`. A blob that fails `sampleDataFits` gives `sampleTooLarge`. Only then `mod_.extraBlob = blob`. `loadSampleFile` reads the file and calls `loadSampleBytes`.

At the end of the file:
```d
bool sampleDataFits(size_t blobBytes) @safe pure nothrow @nogc
private bool buildSamplerExtra(const(ubyte)[] current, uint slot, const(ubyte)[] audio, ubyte root, ubyte low,
        ubyte high, out ubyte[] blob, out string err) @trusted nothrow
private bool readAudioFile(string path, out ubyte[] bytes, out string err) @trusted nothrow
```
`sampleDataFits` returns `blobBytes <= MAX_EXTRA_BLOB_BYTES`. Each adapter wraps one call (`samplerExtraWithSample`, `std.file.read`) in `try`/`catch (Exception ex)`, like `readPresetFile`.

**Steps.** After each step run Gate 2 for the changed file.
1. Add `samplerExtraWithSample` with DDoc.
2. Add the three kinds. Add three `case` lines to the `return false` group of `isNameProblem`.
3. Add imports: `modules.synths.sampler : Sampler, samplerExtraWithSample`; `MAX_EXTRA_BLOB_BYTES` in the `io.project_format` list; `std.file : read`. Add `sampleDataFits` and the two adapters.
4. Add `loadSampleBytes`.
5. Add `loadSampleFile`.
6. Write Tests blocks 1, 2 (two slots loaded 5 then 2; leave the `float.nan` check for Step 7), and 3-7. Run Gate 1 after every two blocks. All tests must pass against the untouched `StudioSession.doLoadSample`.
7. Apply owner decision #1 in `source/app/session.d`: replace lines 3110-3139 of `doLoadSample` with one call to `samplerExtraWithSample` (keeping the signature, `err`, and `doSetModuleExtra` undo step). Then add the `float.nan` WAV check to Test block 2 (before this step, `doLoadSample` did not sanitize NaN samples so the two blobs would differ; after this step both sanitize NaN to `0.0f` and match byte-for-byte). Run Gate 1; every existing sampler, session and sample editor test and the new NaN identity test must pass.
8. Update the file headers (`sampler.d`, `module_writer.d`), run `dub build --compiler=ldc2 --config=compose` (must link cleanly), and run Gates 1, 2, 3.

**Acceptance table.** The WAV is `sineWav(4410, 0.7f)`: mono, 44,100 Hz. Blob size = 8 (magic, count) + 60 per slot (index 4, rate 4, notes 4, loop 16, envelopes 24, frame count 8) + 8 per frame (`serializeExtra`, lines 554-594). Rows 1-6 and the decoder errors were run on 2026-11-26 with a scratch copy.

| Input | Working | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |

tasks.guide:
**Goal.** A new pure module `compose.script.notation` turns note text such as `C4:1 E4:1/2 [C4 E4 G4]:2@0.6 -` into a list of events (offset in lines, length in lines, MIDI pitches, velocity) for a time signature. Every problem is data with its offset in the text. It writes no patterns and knows no commands, parts or `#` comments (T83).

**Read first.**
1. `source/compose/timing.d`: `TimeSignature` (84), `TimingError` (128), `LengthResult` (147), `linesPerBeat` (190), `parseLength` (481-570), `indexOf` (696). Learn the result shape and the sentinel: not found is `text.length`.
2. `source/app/music_theory.d`: `noteName` (234-241), `accidentalText` (328-341). The spelling: letter, `#`/`##`/`b`/`bb`, octave; MIDI 60 is `C4`, 0 is `C-1`, 127 is `G9`. Nothing in the app parses a note name; you write it.
3. `source/sequencer/note.d`: `NoteCell` (75-88), `encodeVelocity` (152), `normalizedVelocity` (280). Notes are MIDI 0..127; velocity is a float 0..1; without one a cell plays at 0.8.
4. `source/app/pattern_notes.d`: `RollNote` (47-54), `addNote` (186-201, velocity in (0, 1]).
5. `tests/unit/compose_timing_test.d`: 27-55 (layout), 406-426 (sweep).

**Existing code to use.**

```d
struct TimeSignature {
    uint numerator = DEFAULT_TIME_SIG_NUMERATOR;
    uint denominator = DEFAULT_TIME_SIG_DENOMINATOR;
    bool isValid() const @safe pure nothrow @nogc
}
struct Length {
    uint lines = 0;
}
struct TimingError {
    size_t offset = 0;
    size_t length = 0;
    string reason = "";
    string suggestion = "";
}
struct LengthResult {
    Length length = Length();
    bool ok = false;
    TimingError error = TimingError();
}
enum ulong MAX_POSITION_LINES = MAX_LINES;
uint linesPerBeat(TimeSignature sig) @safe pure nothrow @nogc
LengthResult parseLength(string text, TimeSignature sig) @safe pure nothrow
string formatTimeSignature(TimeSignature sig) @safe pure nothrow
string noteName(int midi, MusicalKey key) @safe pure nothrow
bool isSpaceChar(char c) @safe pure nothrow @nogc
```

- `linesPerBeat` (timing.d:190) returns 0 for an invalid signature.
- `parseLength` (timing.d:481): on failure `ok` is false and `error.offset` counts from the start of the length text. Empty text is refused. The result is 1 to 4096 lines.
- `MAX_POSITION_LINES` (timing.d:55) is 4096 (`io/project_format.d:59`).
- `noteName` (music_theory.d:234) with `MusicalKey()` spells in C major. `isSpaceChar` is `compose/names.d:220`.
- `RollNote.init.velocity` (pattern_notes.d:52) is 0.8f. Use it; write no second 0.8.
- `LETTER_PITCH` (music_theory.d:62) and `LETTER_PC` (chord_progression.d:128) are private.

**Write.** Grammar, declarations, rules, and every refusal:

```
sequence = [ item { SPACES item } ]
item     = rest | note | chord
rest     = "-" [ ":" length ]
note     = pitch [ ":" length ] [ "@" velocity ]
chord    = "[" pitch { SPACES pitch } "]" [ ":" length ] [ "@" velocity ]
pitch    = LETTER [ "#" | "##" | "b" | "bb" ] [ "-" ] DIGIT { DIGIT }
velocity = DIGIT { DIGIT } [ "." DIGIT { DIGIT } ]     at most 3 digits before the dot, 6 after
length   = any text compose.timing.parseLength accepts
LETTER   = "A" .. "G" (capitals only)
SPACES   = one or more characters for which isSpaceChar is true
```

```d
module compose.script.notation;

import app.music_theory : MusicalKey, noteName;
import app.pattern_notes : RollNote;
import compose.names : isSpaceChar;
import compose.timing : formatTimeSignature, LengthResult, linesPerBeat, MAX_POSITION_LINES, parseLength,
    TimeSignature;

enum float DEFAULT_NOTE_VELOCITY = RollNote.init.velocity;

struct NotationError {
    size_t offset = 0;
    size_t length = 0;
    string reason = "";
    string suggestion = "";
}

struct NoteEvent {
    uint offset = 0;
    uint length = 0;
    ubyte[] pitches;
    float velocity = DEFAULT_NOTE_VELOCITY;
    size_t textOffset = 0;
    size_t textLength = 0;
}

struct PitchResult {
    ubyte midi = 0;
    bool ok = false;
    NotationError error = NotationError();
}

struct NotationResult {
    NoteEvent[] events;
    uint totalLines = 0;
    bool ok = false;
    NotationError error = NotationError();
}

PitchResult parsePitch(string text) @safe pure nothrow
string formatPitch(ubyte midi) @safe pure nothrow
NotationResult parseNotes(string text, TimeSignature sig) @safe pure nothrow

private struct VelocityResult {
    float value = DEFAULT_NOTE_VELOCITY;
    bool ok = false;
    NotationError error = NotationError();
}
private VelocityResult parseVelocity(string text) @safe pure nothrow
private size_t itemEnd(string text, size_t start) @safe pure nothrow @nogc
private size_t findChar(string text, char needle, size_t from) @safe pure nothrow @nogc
private immutable int[7] LETTER_SEMITONES = [9, 11, 0, 2, 4, 5, 7];
```

```
parsePitch     MIDI = (octave + 1) * 12 + LETTER_SEMITONES[letter - 'A'] + accidental
               accidental is +1 for each "#", -1 for each "b"; accepted when 0 <= MIDI <= 127
               error offsets count from the start of the pitch text
formatPitch    noteName(midi, MusicalKey()); "" when midi > 127
parseVelocity  scaled = all digits read as one ulong; divisor = 10 for each digit after the dot
               accepted when 0 < scaled <= divisor
               value = cast(float)(cast(double) scaled / cast(double) divisor)
findChar       index of needle at or after from; text.length when absent
itemEnd        item starts with "[": the first space after its first "]"; text.length when there is no "]"
               any other item: the first space at or after start; text.length when there is none
parseNotes     1. linesPerBeat(sig) == 0: refuse (S1).
               2. carried = linesPerBeat(sig); offset = 0 (ulong).
               3. Skip spaces; take the next item [start .. itemEnd).
               4. head = "[" up to and including "]" for a chord; otherwise the text before the first ":" or "@".
                  The rest of the item is the suffix: [":" length]["@" velocity].
               5. head == "-" is a rest. Otherwise parsePitch(head), or parsePitch of each pitch inside "[ ]".
               6. A written length: parseLength; carried = its lines. No written length: length = carried.
                  This holds for notes, chords and rests alike.
               7. "@velocity" applies to the whole chord. No "@": DEFAULT_NOTE_VELOCITY. Velocity is never carried.
               8. offset + length > MAX_POSITION_LINES: refuse (S8).
               9. Note or chord: append NoteEvent(offset, length, pitches in written order, velocity, start, item length).
                  Rest: append nothing.
               10. offset += length; go to 3. At the end: ok = true, totalLines = offset.
               Empty or all-space text: ok, no events, totalLines 0.
               First problem: return ok = false, events empty, the error with offsets in the whole text.
```

**Pitfalls.**
- `-` is a rest and also the minus of `C-1`. A rest is only `head == "-"`.
- The pattern editor shows middle C as `C-4` (`gui/views/pattern_editor.d:123`). Here `C-4` means octave −4.

- `std.conv.to` and `std.format` do not compile in `nothrow`; `indexOf` and `isDigit` in `timing.d` are private. Write loops.

tasks.title: Composition helper: parts, sections, and arrangement
tasks.done: 2026-11-26 (owner accepted the proposal). Recorded here until T89 moves it into `docs/manual.md` and `../architecture.md`. A part is one voice: a name bound to one module (for example "bass"); a drum part is bound to a set of lanes instead. A section is a named stretch of music with a length in bars ("verse", 8 bars). Each part has one pattern per section it plays in, named "*part* · *section*"; notes of a part are written into its section pattern and the helper adds tracker tracks as needed (as the piano roll does); drum parts get drum patterns. `arrange` lists the sections in order, each part gets its own timeline lane, a section that appears twice reuses the same pattern (a clone clip), and the loop covers the whole arrangement unless set otherwise. A script may skip sections for short pieces: writing to a part without naming a section uses one implicit section as long as the music written.

tasks.title: Module writer: defects found in review
tasks.task:
Fix the defects a review of T74 found in `ModuleWriter`, each with a test that fails first. Until then T75 and T76 would build on them.
  - A copy of a writer shares its parameter values with the original (`auto c = w; c.setParamValue(…)` changes `w`): give the struct a copy constructor that copies the values, and test that copies are independent.
  - A too-long name is cut in the middle of a character, and the suggested name (invalid UTF-8) is then accepted by `setName()`: cut at a character boundary.
  - `setName()` accepts names the instrument library refuses (`Keys/Lead`, `.hidden`, `a:b`): use `app.instrument_library.isValidPresetName` instead of the second copy of the rule. Names taken from a preset or a file name pass the same check.
  - A huge value on a discrete parameter (`setParamValue("…", 1e30f)`) is reported as `9223372036854775807` through an undefined cast: guard the conversion as the continuous path does.
  - A number too large for a float (`1e40`) is reported as "not a number" without a suggestion: report it as out of range with the nearest value.
  - `textOf()` must always give text `setParamText()` accepts, also when an option name looks like a number (T91 adds many option names): write the number in that case, and test it.
  - A preset with an empty preset name is not named as the app names it (the app keeps the module's own name), and the test asserts the wrong behaviour.
  - Values loaded from a preset are not checked against the parameter's range: report them or document why not.
  - `nearestTypeName()` prefers any type id over a closer display name, against its own description.
  - The edit distance and nearest-name helpers exist twice (`compose/module_writer.d`, `compose_main.d`): move them to one shared module in `source/compose/`.
  - Tests to tighten: the assertions that only check that a reason or a suggestion exists; the unused "matches more than one type" and `writeFailed` paths; a unique temporary folder name.

tasks.guide:
**Goal.** SpectraVoice *Profile* and *Bandwidth* change the sound at once: from the rack, automation, MIDI, and on loading a project or preset. `prepare()` builds all 172 tables off the audio thread; `process()` only picks one. Left out: changes to `session.d`, a crossfade (T115).

**Read first.**
1. `source/modules/synths/spectravoice.d`: `buildHarmonicTable` (74-150), `serializeExtra` (357-366), `deserializeExtra` (394-421), `prepare` (442-449), `process` (547-578), `swapAsset` (591-599), `selectedProfile` (601-607).
2. `source/graph/registry.d` `createOffRT` (168-191), `source/app/session.d` `instantiateSavedModule` (4252-4264). `prepare()` runs once, with the defaults, before the saved parameters are set. So today every SpectraVoice plays Organ at 0.35, also after reopening.
3. `source/sequencer/track_effects.d:374`, `source/sequencer/engine.d:1163`. Automation and MIDI set parameters on the audio thread. Nothing tells the UI thread.
4. `source/app/session.d` `setModuleExtraDirect` (3539-3563), `source/graph/module_api.d` `buildAssetsFromExtraImpl` (546-576). The only asset swap path. It starts from extra data, never from a parameter.
5. `tests/unit/modules_test.d` 163-173, 378-439. Every `setParam` runs under the allocation trap.

**Existing code to use.**
```d
static SpectraTableAsset* buildHarmonicTable(uint profile, float bandwidth, size_t tableSize = 2048)
```
`spectravoice.d:74`. Null on a bad size or no memory. `@nogc nothrow`. Keep signature and result.
```d
static bool tryAllocate(size_t count, out OwnedBuffer!T result, size_t alignment = DEFAULT_SIMD_ALIGNMENT)
static void inverse(T[] realPart, T[] imagPart)
```
`foundation/memory.d:113`: false when out of memory; `result` is `out`; floats start at zero. `dsp/fft.d:147`: `@nogc nothrow pure @safe`, in place; call `FftFloat.inverse`.
```d
bool function(void*, uint paramIdx, float val, float sampleRate, bool instant) @nogc nothrow setParam;
bool function(void*, ref ProcessIO io, ref ProcessContext ctx) @nogc nothrow process;
bool function(void*, uint slot, void* newAsset, out void* oldAsset) @nogc nothrow swapAsset;
static bool createOffRT(string typeId, ModuleId id, float sampleRate, out ModuleInstance instance)
void verifyZeroRtAllocationsNothrow(scope void delegate() @nogc nothrow rtStep)
```
`graph/module_api.d:114`, `111`, `116`; `graph/registry.d:205`; `tests/rt_malloc_trap.d:299`. Parameter 0 is Profile, 1 is Bandwidth. `setParam` clamps (lines 435-441). `oldAsset` is `out`.

**Write.** In `spectravoice.d`, before `struct SpectraVoiceSlot` (line 170):
```d
float clampBandwidth(float bandwidth) @nogc nothrow pure @safe
size_t harmonicCount(float bandwidth) @nogc nothrow pure @safe
void fillHarmonicTable(float[] tbl, float[] re, float[] im, uint profile, size_t harmonics) @nogc nothrow
```
`clampBandwidth` is lines 91-92. `harmonicCount` returns `cast(size_t)(4.0 + cast(double) clampBandwidth(bandwidth) * 44.0)` (line 94). `fillHarmonicTable` sets `re[] = 0.0f; im[] = 0.0f;`, then runs lines 93 and 95-139 unchanged, with `tableSize = tbl.length` and `activeHarmonics = harmonics`. `buildHarmonicTable` keeps its allocations and lines 141-149 and calls these.
```d
struct SpectraTableBank {
    enum size_t TABLE_SIZE = 2048;
    enum size_t PROFILE_COUNT = 4;
    enum size_t MIN_HARMONICS = 6;
    enum size_t MAX_HARMONICS = 48;
    enum size_t COUNTS_PER_PROFILE = MAX_HARMONICS - MIN_HARMONICS + 1;
    enum size_t TABLE_COUNT = PROFILE_COUNT * COUNTS_PER_PROFILE;
    OwnedBuffer!float tables;
    @disable this(this);
    static SpectraTableBank* build() @nogc nothrow
    const(float)[] table(uint profile, float bandwidth) const @nogc nothrow
    static void destroyErased(void* raw) @nogc nothrow
}
```
`build()` allocates `TABLE_COUNT * TABLE_SIZE` floats and two work buffers, and fills table `p * COUNTS_PER_PROFILE + (count - MIN_HARMONICS)` for each profile and count; null when out of memory. `table()` clamps the profile to 3 and the count to 6..48 and returns that 2048-float slice (null for an empty bank). Destructor as in `SpectraTableAsset` (lines 59-61, 158-164).

In `struct SpectraVoice`:
```d
static immutable ubyte[4] CUSTOM_TABLE_MAGIC = ['S', 'V', 'T', '1'];
private SpectraTableBank* bank_ = null;
private const(float)[] activeTable() const @nogc nothrow
```
- `activeTable()`: the slot-0 table when `tableAsset_` is not null and not empty; else `bank_.table(selectedProfile(), bandwidth)`; null without a bank.
- `prepare()`: builds `bank_` when null; no longer builds `tableAsset_`.
- `~this()`: also frees `bank_`.
- `process()`: reads `activeTable()` once; silence when its length is below 2.
- `serializeExtra`: the payload is the 4 magic bytes, then the floats.
- `deserializeExtra`: if `payload.length < 4 || payload[0 .. 4] != CUSTOM_TABLE_MAGIC[]`, treat it as empty or an old stored table: return true, install nothing. Else check and copy `payload[4 .. $]` as today (must be `>= 64 * float.sizeof` and a multiple of `float.sizeof`).

2. Add `SpectraTableBank`.
3. Add `bank_`, `activeTable()`; change `prepare()`, `~this()`, `process()`.
4. Add the magic to `serializeExtra` and `deserializeExtra`.
5. `modules_test.d:437`: change `oldSpec !is null` to `oldSpec is null`. Line 438 stays.

(1) "limiter reached" is reported only for samples at 0.999 or more after the soft limiter, which starts at 0.95, so a mix driven to about twice full scale still says "limiter not reached" (a Saw Lead with 4-voice chords and a Synth Bass, both at gain 1 into `out`). Report when the limiter engages (input above its threshold), with the number of bars affected. (2) `render` follows a custom `loop` (for example `loop verse chorus`), so the end of the arrangement is never heard; T68 says the loop covers the arrangement unless set otherwise. Decide with the owner whether `render` plays the arrangement once from start to end (proposed) or the loop, and state it in the report header. Tests for both.
tasks.done: 2026-11-27. Owner decision 2026-11-27: render plays the arrangement once from start to end. render switches the loop off for its session, states 'the arrangement once from start to end' in the header, and prints 'Loop: lines a to b, not followed by the render' for a custom loop (JSON: playback, loop.start/end/followed). The limiter counts as engaged when an output sample passes LIMITER_KNEE (0.95, now a named constant in modules/output.d), with limiterBars and a per-bar (limiter) mark. Tests in tests/unit/compose_song_checks_test.d; docs/composer.md §4.4 and §7.2, architecture §10.2. Recorded in docs/changelog.md.

tasks.title: Error messages: wrong suggestions and empty section names
tasks.task: Found while writing `docs/composer.md` (T89). (1) A chord progression longer than its section is reported at the command word with "did you mean '1'?", a position shown as a name suggestion; report it at the progression with the section length and the number of bars the progression needs. (2) `notes` or `chords` without a section once sections exist says "there is no section ''; did you mean 'a'?"; say that a section is needed and list the sections. (3) `describe` prints raw `arrange clip=#id` lines when parts were declared in another order than it uses, although the arrangement is a plain section arrangement; print `arrange <sections>` then. Tests for each message.
tasks.done: 2026-11-27. (1) A chord progression longer than its named section is refused before writing, at the progression: 'the progression needs 4 bars, but section a has 2 bars; lengthen the section (section a bars=4) or shorten the progression' (ChordProblemKind.progressionTooLong). (2) A missing section name says 'a section is needed here, because the song has sections (a, b); write the section after the part name', at the part name, without a suggestion. (3) Reopened melodic parts are ordered by their timeline lanes, so describe prints arrange <sections> for a plain arrangement whatever order the notes were written in. Tests in tests/unit/compose_song_checks_test.d and compose_part_test.d. Recorded in docs/changelog.md.

tasks.title: Notes that last to the end of a pattern are never released
tasks.task: Found while testing T118. A note that ends exactly at the end of its pattern gets no note-off (the note-off would fall on the line after the pattern: part_writer.d and pattern_notes.d write it only when end < lines), and the sequencer does not release notes when a clip ends. The note therefore holds at full level through any following gap and through the 2-second render tail, until a later note on the same track replaces it. Reproduce: section a bars=1, section rest bars=2, notes mel a: C4:4, arrange a rest; render reports bars 2 and 3 at average 0.094 (C4:15l leaves bar 3 silent). This affects songs made in the app as well. Owner to choose: (a) the engine sends a note-off for the notes a clip started when that clip ends (changes playback of existing projects, in the app too); (b) the composition helper and the piano roll end such notes one line early; (c) leave it and keep the workaround documented in docs/composer.md §9.
